prompt: Write an email to a colleague about the weather spoiling your garden plans. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the email only.
final_message:
**Subject: Garden plans washed out (again)**

Hi Priya,

I hope your week is going better than mine, at least weather-wise! I wanted to share my frustration with you, since I know you've been following my garden project with such patience.

You'll remember that I'd set aside this past weekend to finally get the autumn planting done. I had everything lined up: the garlic cloves sorted and ready, a dozen bags of compost delivered, and the new raised bed frames waiting to be assembled. I'd even booked Friday afternoon off so I could get a head start while the soil was still workable. Then the forecast changed, and it has been pouring ever since.

It started Thursday night and hasn't really let up. By Saturday morning the back lawn looked more like a pond than a garden, and the beds I'd already dug over were completely waterlogged. I did venture out in my wellies for an hour on Sunday, hoping for a break in the clouds, but all I managed to do was track mud through the kitchen and nearly lose a boot in the vegetable patch. The compost bags are sitting under a tarp by the shed, and I suspect the garlic is going to be late this year, which is not ideal given how much I was looking forward to it.

The worst part is that the forecast for the coming week doesn't look much better. There's a brief dry spell predicted for Wednesday, but then more rain is due to roll in by the weekend. If the ground stays this saturated, I'm worried about the roots rotting before anything has a chance to establish. I may have to rethink the whole schedule and move some of the planting into early spring instead, which feels like a bit of a defeat after all the preparation.

Still, I'm trying to look on the bright side. The rain barrels are completely full, so I'll have plenty of water for next summer, and it has given me time to finalize the layout for the new beds. I've been sketching out a rotation plan indoors, which is a surprisingly relaxing way to spend a gloomy afternoon.

If you have any tips for dealing with waterlogged soil, I'd love to hear them. I know you had a similar problem a couple of years ago and managed to rescue your beds. Perhaps we could chat over coffee on Thursday? I'll bring some photos of the damage, and you can tell me whether it's as bad as it looks.

Hope you're staying dry!

Best wishes,
[name]
